The contrasting position reasserts design as a materially grounded practice. Here knowledge is generated through embodied making, through the resistance and affordances of materials, and through the sociotechnical infrastructures that condition what is actually possible. Rather than treating discourse as primary, this view emphasises discourse as material like everything else. What matter are the specific crafting skills designers have for shaping infrascture of material and meaning togehter. Design becomes a practice of pragmatically negotiating reality itself as it pushes back against or redirect idealistic/fascistic narratives. What matters are empirical observational methods for evaluating real impacts in the world

One position understands design as a fundamentally discursive, language-centred practice. Here design’s power lies in the narratives, metaphors and vocabularies that organise attention and mobilise publics. Strategies, briefs, and visions function as rhetorical devices that construct problems and futures long before anything material is made. In this view, design operates by shaping meaning, aligning actors and projecting desirable horizons, with its effectiveness measured through persuasion, coherence and cultural traction rather than through material outcomes.
